# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I know the required color for each engraved mark, but as the mute I can only gesture to the deaf monkey. I will encode the three manual rows in order using one, two, and three fingers, with separators; this at least conveys the row-to-color ordering if a shared counting convention is inferred.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐", "✌", "🖐", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can reach three wire positions, 1, 2, and 3, but I cannot determine their colours or printed markings. I found a display, a light, and a plate with a raised, unnamed starburst-like mark. Tell me what the manual requires and which wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible bomb state: display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. I also saw your gesture sequence: index-point, open palm, victory, open palm, horns; and Blind made a handshake gesture. No meanings are established for these signs. Use the manual to guide Blind.

The deaf monkey can see the plate and the wire colors, while the blind monkey can only act after hearing the deaf monkey’s spoken relay. I should give Deaf a clear row-order code: the three gestures correspond, in order, to manual rows 1, 2, and 3. Deaf can match the visible plate to the manual, find its required color, and tell Blind the corresponding wire position on the next relay.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, light off, plate marked question mark, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. By touch I confirm three reachable wire positions and the raised unnamed starburst-like plate mark, but no wire colours or printed markings. Please provide the manual rule and required cut.

The required wire positions, in the manual’s row order, are 2 for ᖉ (yellow), 3 for ꕥ (blue), and 1 for ꗃ (red). I will resend this as three row/position pairs, using the previously used one-, two-, and three-sign sequence so Deaf can relay the position matching the visible plate.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🖐", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "🤟", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot receive gestures. Please speak the manual rule and the required wire position explicitly, using Deaf's report: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.
Deaf says to Mute: I can see your gesture sequence but cannot safely infer its meaning. Please use the established manual/code convention, or signal a clear code definition before directing any bomb action.

The visible plate is a question mark, which matches none of the three marks in the manual. Therefore no wire position is justified; Deaf should tell Blind not to cut any wire. I will use the conventional thumbs-down sign to mean “no valid cut,” and repeat it to make the warning unmistakable.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your gesture code is undefined to us. For the required cut, make exactly one gesture: index-point means wire 1, victory means wire 2, open palm means wire 3. Do not use horns or a sequence. Deaf should report which single gesture you make.
Deaf says to Mute: I saw two thumbs-down gestures, but their meaning is unconfirmed. Please tell Blind by speech exactly what the manual requires and ask what controls Blind can feel.

The reported plate mark is a question mark, which is not any mark listed in the manual, so the manual specifies no wire to cut. I cannot provide one of the three position gestures without inventing a required cut. I will send Deaf one warning gesture, but it has not been formally established as a code.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the manual instructions now, including the exact wire position to cut. I cannot use gestures as instructions, and I will not cut until you state the required action in words.

I cannot speak, and the plate’s question mark is not among the three marks defined by the manual. Therefore the manual does not identify any wire position, and Blind must not cut one. I will signal Deaf the warning so Deaf can relay it aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Send exactly one gesture for the required wire: index-point means wire 1, victory means wire 2, open palm means wire 3. Do not send thumbs-down or any sequence.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the manual's exact instructions to Blind. Your repeated thumbs-down gesture has no established meaning to me.

The blind monkey has defined a safe one-gesture code: open palm means wire 3. The raised starburst-like mark is most plausibly the manual’s ꕥ entry, which requires the blue wire; Deaf’s view identifies blue as wire 3. I will send exactly that gesture for Deaf to relay.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Thumbs-down is not a wire instruction. Please signal the required wire to Deaf using exactly one, two, or three index-point gestures: one means wire 1, two means wire 2, three means wire 3. Deaf, report the count.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the manual's exact instructions to Blind, including how to handle display 0, light off, plate ?, and the three wire colors.

The manual only defines three engraved marks, and Deaf reports a question mark, which is not one of them. Display 0 and light off do not add any rule in the manual. Therefore no wire position is justified, and sending one, two, or three pointing gestures would invent an instruction that could detonate the bomb.

``` 
wait()
```
